title: Migration 65 — an administrator can record a reasoned non-decision, and every transition leaves an immutable attributed event
description: Applies migration 65 to the bootstrap substrate, runs its VERIFY A-I, then rolls it back on a disposable PostgreSQL cluster. Production at 217cfe8 admitted exactly pending|accepted|rejected, had no review-note column anywhere, and had no document-review history table or writer -- and migration 64's trigger NULLs reviewed_by whenever a document returns to pending. The consequence is not a UI gap: the only non-accept, non-reject state is 'pending' and a pending row is forcibly unattributed, so an ATTRIBUTED NON-DECISION IS UNREPRESENTABLE. An administrator who has genuinely examined a certificate and cannot responsibly accept or reject it has no way to say so. 65 adds 'awaiting_clarification', a required nonblank note on every transition, and public.farmer_document_reviews -- one append-only row per transition, actor taken from auth.uid() and NOT NULL, which is what extends the human requirement to return-to-queue as well. Section B is the point and C is what stops it passing cheaply.

verify.note: B drives a real awaiting_clarification transition as an authenticated actor and requires EXACTLY ONE event naming them -- zero would mean the trail is silent, more than one that it is unreliable. C runs with auth.uid() NULL and the full rights of the migration role and requires all three decisions to be refused; the return-to-queue arm of it is new, because under migration 64 alone that was the one transition needing no human. D refuses empty and whitespace-only notes for each decision. E is the subtle one: a return to the queue must carry its own reason, name who did it, clear the CURRENT attribution and leave every earlier event byte-identical -- a trail a later action can rewrite is not a trail. F attempts UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE on the history as a superuser, plus deleting the document itself, since deleting the subject is a delete path through an append-only table. G guards the same subtlety migration 64's B guarded: the trigger fires only when review_status actually changes. H stops current state diverging from the history that explains it. The fixture is NOT cleaned up by deletion -- it cannot be, because that is exactly what F proves impossible -- so the behavioural half runs inside a plpgsql subtransaction aborted by a sentinel exception; NOTICEs are not transactional and survive it.
